hook_text: It takes more than a hundred years to make one centimetre of soil. One storm can wash it away in an afternoon.
clip_script: Everything you eat starts in soil, a thin skin of crushed rock, rotting leaves, air, water and tiny living things. It forms painfully slowly. Now picture a hillside where too many cattle have eaten all the grass. A thunderstorm hits. The bare soil washes away, carving a donga, and the mud fills the dam downstream. The same story plays out with water polluted by sewage and old mine water, and with air filled with smoke from coal. Water, air and soil are renewable only if we treat them well.
visual_style: A time-lapse of soil layers slowly building; then a storm hits a bare hillside and a gully opens; quick cuts to a polluted river and a smoky power station skyline.
pacing: Slow build, sudden storm, steady close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on natural resources and how we use them.
